newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fresh economic factors fail to impress Bund market.
newsitem.headline: Fresh economic factors fail to impress Bund market.

text.p: Bund futures digested a mound of economic news on Tuesday but at the end of the day found little reason to stray far from where they opened.
Traders said the market is unlikely to break out of the range seen so far this week until Thursday at the soonest when German unemployment and gross domestic product data are to be released.
And even then traders may decide to keep their powder dry until all-important U.S. jobs data are released Friday.
At 1433 GMT, the DTB Bund future was up two basis points at 99.58, having traded in a range between 99.32 and 99.75.
"Initially, people expected news we have seen today to hold the market back," said Stuart Trow, manager of market analysis at Norinchukin International Plc. "But ranges have prevailed."
The market had only faint reaction to a report from the DIW research institute which showed the think-tank had cut its 1997 German GDP growth forecast to two percent from 2.5 percent.
The short-end of the yield curve was hurt early on when Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said in a newspaper interview that he saw no need to change interest rates for the time being.
German industrial orders, meanwhile climbed 0.5 percent in November from the month before. Economists said the figures pointed to moderate economic growth.
The German government also issued five billion marks of a new 10-year, six percent coupon bond to the Federal Bond Consortium.
The bond was priced at 101.05 and the yield is 5.86 percent. A second tranche of the bond will be issued in an auction with bids due by 1000 GMT on Wednesday.
The most important German indicator due this week is December unemployment data at 0900 GMT.
Economists said they expect ann increase of between 35,000 to 60,000 from November's record 4.1 million. "The trend will remain unbroken," Goldman Sachs economist Thomas Mayer said.
Traders said a higher unemployment figure will help Bunds by renewing hopes for a cut in the repo rate.

Bunds strongly outperformed T-notes late in the day, pushing the spread to 71 basis points from 66 basis points at the prior close. Traders said while Bunds should continue to perform better than U.S. debt, the spread was unlikely to widen beyond 80 basis points-- the upper end of a long-running range.
The yield curve, meanwhile, continued its recent steepening trend with the spread between 2- and 10-year Bunds widening four basis points to 244.
Most of the gain came on the short-end where the spread between 2- and 5-year Bunds added three basis points to 145 basis points.
